function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity as a natural phenomenon has been known since ancient times (e.g., static electricity observed by Thales of Miletus). Its systematic study began with William Gilbert in the 16th century, who coined the term “electricus.” Key discoveries that led to modern electrical science include Benjamin Franklin’s kite experiment (mid‑1700s), Alessandro Volta’s invention of the voltaic pile (1800), Michael Faraday’s work on electromagnetic induction (1831), and James Clerk Maxwell’s equations (1860s). Thus, electricity wasn’t discovered by a single individual but rather developed through contributions from many scientists over centuries.
